Okay, so you have to call customer service here. Let me save you an hour. First, you never get a person right away. You get an automated menu: press one for billing, press two for technical support, and so on. If you want to get through to a real person faster, just say representative, two or three times, and the machine usually gives up. Second, before you call, have your account number ready, and when the rep answers, ask for a case number right away. Write it down. If the call drops, you don't have to start from zero. Third, expect to be on hold. I've been calling my phone company for years, and my record is fifty-five minutes. Put them on speaker and do the dishes. And if the rep can't solve the problem, don't hang up. Ask politely: could you escalate this, or could I speak to a supervisor? That one sentence has saved me more money than any coupon.

Hi, this message is for Gisele Gallego. This is Kevin from Capitol Fiber, returning your call about case number four, seven, two, nine, one. I'm sorry for the wait. I know you've been trying to get through to us since last Monday. So, here's the update. We've been looking at your account, and you're right: you were charged twice for October. That was a billing error on our side. I escalated it to my supervisor yesterday, and she approved a full refund of eighty-nine dollars. It's going to take five to seven business days to show up on your card. You don't need to do anything else. If you have any questions, call us back and give them the case number, so you don't have to explain everything again. Have a great day.

I used to yell at customer service. Here is what I learned after years of being fed up with companies. The person on the phone is not the company. The rep didn't make the billing error, and they didn't write that automated menu either. When you yell, they follow the script, and you get the runaround: let me transfer you, please hold, let me transfer you again. When you're calm, they start working for you. So now I say three things. My name. What I've been trying to do, and for how long: I've been calling about this for a week. And what I want: a refund, a technician, a date. Then I say thank you, and I mean it. And if nothing works, I don't hang up angry. I ask for a supervisor, I write down the case number, and I call again the next day. Patience is not weakness. On the phone, it's a strategy.
